patterns.platform: Webflow / Framer hero text baked into an exported image or background
patterns.name: Images of text in hero/banner graphics
patterns.description: To preserve exact typography, designers export a hero headline, promotional banner, or pricing graphic as a flattened PNG/JPG (or set it as a CSS background-image) instead of live text. The 'text' is pixels: it can't be resized/restyled, and if alt is missing or generic the content is also lost to screen readers.
patterns.whyAutoToolsMiss: Nothing in the markup declares that an image's pixels contain readable text; an automated tool can't OCR/decide an image is 'an image of text' that could have been real text (1.4.5) vs. a legitimate photo/logo. Even an image with alt passes 1.1.1 — judging it's text-as-image needs human visual inspection.
patterns.realWorldNote: Design-to-site workflows commonly flatten styled headlines to images to preserve fonts; 1.4.5 prohibits images of text except logos/essential cases: https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG21/Understanding/images-of-text.html

patterns.platform: Banner/promo graphics, pricing tables, infographics rendered as flat images on Wix/Squarespace/Mailchimp landing pages
patterns.name: Images of text carrying essential information with no text equivalent
patterns.description: Headlines, sale terms, pricing tables, and event details are baked into a single flattened JPG/PNG (often exported from Canva/Figma). The alt text, if any, is a short label that omits the embedded copy, so the actual information (prices, dates, fine print) is unavailable non-visually and pixelates/blurs on zoom.
patterns.whyAutoToolsMiss: No automated tool performs OCR to discover that an image contains essential text, nor that the alt fails to reproduce it. Recognizing 'this picture is really a block of text and the alt drops the price/date' requires a human to read both the image and the alt and compare.
patterns.realWorldNote: Images-of-text is a perennial manual-audit and VPAT partial-support item; tied to the alt-text gap WebAIM measures: https://webaim.org/projects/million/2025 . Litigation grounding: the Robles v. Domino's case turned on screen-reader-inaccessible image/graphic content: https://www.boia.org/blog/the-robles-v.-dominos-settlement-and-why-it-matters

patterns.platform: Marketing hero banners / promo slides in CMS slideshows (Shopify slideshow, Squarespace banner, email-style heroes)
patterns.name: Headline baked into a hero image (image of text)
patterns.description: The campaign headline, price, and CTA wording are composited into a single hero JPG/PNG by a designer, then placed with a generic or empty alt. The visible "text" pixelates on zoom, can't be restyled for users who need larger/high-contrast type, and is either unreadable to AT (empty alt) or crammed into one alt string. Often the same banner is the page's only H1-level content, so the heading is also an image.
patterns.whyAutoToolsMiss: An empty-alt decorative image passes 1.1.1 trivially, and a non-empty alt passes too — tools cannot OCR the image to discover it contains essential text that should have been live HTML, nor judge whether that text is "essential" (logo) versus avoidable. Detecting text-in-image and deciding it's a 1.4.5 violation is a visual/semantic call.
patterns.realWorldNote: Compositing headline text into hero images is a documented 1.4.5 failure; fix is extracting to HTML/CSS overlay. https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/images-of-text.html and https://testparty.ai/blog/wcag-1-4-5-images-of-text-2025-guide
